title: How Does a Kingdom Collapse?

voice.direction: A calm, clear guide tracing a chain of events, never doom-laden. The hook is gently contrarian. Each 'So…' line is plain and a touch quicker than the last, as if the chain is gathering speed. 'Then the emperor dies with two heirs' is quiet and matter-of-fact: the small thing. The lesson is slow and sure; the CTA a friendly, real question. No trailer voice.

lines.text: Empires rarely fall because one person woke up and decided to be evil.
Usually, it starts with a bad harvest.
So taxes rise, and collectors skim more.
So the provinces refuse to pay.
So the army marches out, and feeding it empties the granaries.
Then the emperor dies with two heirs.
No single crack brings down an empire. Cracks that feed each other do.
Which would destroy your empire first: famine, civil war, or corruption?

shots.purpose: The mechanism: the four cracks are one loop. Feeding the army empties the granaries, so famine starts it again, faster each lap, until one ordinary event (a death with two heirs) splits the empire's seal. Then the shareable thought.
shots.visual: Four medallions (the plates) on a ring around the empire's seal; arrows join them and the last arrow closes the loop back to FAMINE; a pulse runs round faster and faster, cracks spreading through the seal on every pass; on 'two heirs' the seal splits in two. The loop lifts; 'NO SINGLE CRACK / Cracks that feed each other do.'

shots.lighting: Dimmed and cooled under the diagram.
shots.onScreenText: Ring FAMINE → CORRUPTION → REVOLT → OVERREACH → FAMINE around the seal of TOLMERE; then 'NO SINGLE CRACK' / 'Cracks that feed each other do.'
shots.transition: Dissolve (0.6 s) to the capital at dusk.
shots.music: C minor driving, then a held breath on the split; A-flat to C major on the lesson.

shots.music: A-flat to C major, warm; fades fully before the last frame.

lesson: Collapse is a feedback loop, not a villain or a single disaster. Economic strain, corruption, revolt, military overreach, succession crises and lost legitimacy each make the next worse, until an ordinary event breaks a system that's already cracked.

music.key: C minor, resolving to C major
